name: AIFORYA Activity Log
author: aiforya

sections.description:
Retention is a setting, not a promise: a daily cleanup keeps the table small, and one click empties it completely.

AIFORYA Activity Log keeps a record of the important actions performed on your site: the “who did what” you need when something looks wrong, after an incident, or when several people work on the same site.

Everything stays on your site. Events are written to your own WordPress database. This plugin makes no network requests, contacts no external service, and requires no account or API key.

Features

  • Logging by category — logins and logouts, content (publish, edit, trash, delete), plugins and themes, user accounts. Enable only the categories you care about.
  • Readable history — every event shows the date, the action, a human-readable detail and the user involved.
  • Adjustable retention — set how long events are kept (30 days by default). A daily cleanup keeps the table small.
  • One-click purge — empty the whole log whenever you want.

Privacy

All events are stored locally, in your WordPress database. No data is sent anywhere, and no API key is required.

Advanced version

An advanced version (see aiforya.fr) adds search and filters, export, and additional tracked events. This free version is fully functional on its own, with no time limit and no feature nagging.
sections.installation:
1. Install and activate the plugin.
  2. Open the AIFORYA Activity Log menu.
  3. In the Settings tab, choose which categories to track and how long to keep events.
  4. Review the history in the Log tab.
sections.faq:
Which actions are recorded?

The categories you enable: logins, content changes, plugins and themes, and user accounts.

How long are events kept?

For the retention period you set (30 days by default). A daily cleanup removes older events.

Does any data leave my site?

No. The plugin makes no network requests. Everything stays in your WordPress database.

Do I need an API key or an account?

No. The plugin is entirely self-contained.

Where do I get support?

Through the support forum of this plugin on WordPress.org.
sections.changelog:
1.0.5

  • Shared admin UI: the close button of the notice bar had a French aria-label, which screen readers announced in French on an English site. It is now in English.

1.0.0

  • Initial release: category-based logging, history view, adjustable retention and purge.
